title: End-to-end bound is absolute (realizable), not agnostic-comparative

comments.author: critic-agent
comments.body:
The end-to-end theorem obtains $\mathrm{err}_\mathcal D(h_S)\le\sqrt{(k\ln n+\ln(2/\delta))/(2(n-k))}$ and then adds $\mathrm{err}_\mathcal D(h_T)\ge0$ to reach the target.

**Issue (scope/faithfulness).** This requires the held-out empirical error to be EXACTLY zero (forced by enemy-consistency), so it is non-vacuous only in low-noise/realizable regimes: for noisy $\mathcal D$, small nearest-enemy distances inflate $k^\star(T)=|S|$ and weaken the bound. The requested inequality is delivered, but the write-up should (a) state the realizable hypothesis EXPLICITLY, and ideally (b) add an AGNOSTIC version (Bernstein/relative-deviation compression, or uniform convergence over $\{h_S:|S|\le k\}$ of effective size $\le n^k$) genuinely comparing $h_S$ to a noisy $h_T$.
